edition.witness_note: Lake 1912 Loeb copy-text; Lightfoot/Funk middle recension not yet locked as second witness

source_text: [1] Τέκνα οὖν φωτὸς ἀληθείας, φεύγετε τὸν μερισμὸν καὶ τὰς κακοδιδασκαλίας: ὅπου δὲ ὁ ποιμήν ἐστιν, ἐκεῖ ὡς πρόβατα ἀκολουθεῖτε. [2] πολλοὶ γὰρ λύκοι ἀξιόπιστοι ἡδονῇ κακῇ αἰχμαλωτίζουσιν τοὺς θεοδρόμους: ἀλλ’ ἐν τῇ ἑνότητι ὑμῶν οὐχ ἕξουσιν τόπον.
pass_a_gloss: So, children of the light of truth, flee division and evil teachings; and where the shepherd is, follow there as sheep. For many wolves who seem trustworthy take captive, by evil pleasure, those who run God's race; but in your unity they will find no place.
pass_b_english: You are children of the light of truth (Ephesians 5:8), so run from division and from evil teaching. Wherever the shepherd is, be there, following like sheep. Many wolves wear a trustworthy face, and with wicked pleasure they carry off as captives those who are running toward God. But in your unity they will have no room.

choices.english: those who are running toward God
choices.why: Ignatius's coinage for runners in God's race.
rejected: those that are running towards God (kept close in sense, reworded)

choices.why: Seeming credible is the danger; a short image keeps the bite.
Genitive chain, not two coordinate nouns.

anf_compare.notes: Same sense. ANF 'children of light and truth' turns the genitive chain into a pair.

notes: 'Take captive' (αἰχμαλωτίζουσιν) may echo 2 Timothy 3:6, which ANF tags; only the verb is shared, so it is not cited inline.
Wolves among sheep may recall Matthew 7:15, Acts 20:29, and John 10; general imagery, not cited inline.

review.notes: Checked paragraph [1] only. Τέκνα οὖν φωτὸς ἀληθείας, φεύγετε τὸν μερισμὸν καὶ τὰς κακοδιδασκαλίας is Pass A 'So, children of the light of truth, flee division and evil teachings' and Pass B 'You are children of the light of truth (Ephesians 5:8), so run from division and from evil teaching'. ὅπου δὲ ὁ ποιμήν ἐστιν, ἐκεῖ ὡς πρόβατα ἀκολουθεῖτε is A 'where the shepherd is, follow there as sheep' and B 'Wherever the shepherd is, be there, following like sheep'. πολλοὶ γὰρ λύκοι ἀξιόπιστοι ἡδονῇ κακῇ αἰχμαλωτίζουσιν τοὺς θεοδρόμους keeps wolf agency and the captives as τοὺς θεοδρόμους in A 'wolves who seem trustworthy take captive, by evil pleasure' and B 'with wicked pleasure they carry off as captives'. ἀλλ’ ἐν τῇ ἑνότητι ὑμῶν οὐχ ἕξουσιν τόπον stays future denial in A 'they will find no place' and B 'they will have no room'. (Ephesians 5:8) matches the supplied τέκνα φωτός wording tag, not a shifted verse. Title 'Where the Shepherd Is' names the shepherd clause.

Source identity confirmed: Greek matches Ignatius Philadelphians 2 from Lake 1912 Loeb. Completeness: all clauses from both Greek sentences rendered. Negation: 'οὐχ ἕξουσιν τόπον' correctly rendered as 'they will have no room'. Agency: wolves (subject) take captive (verb) the god-runners (object) preserved. Modality: indicative mood maintained. Doctrine: unity as protective preserve matches Ignatian ecclesiology. Scripture: Ephesians 5:8 correctly identified as allusion via wording 'ὡς τέκνα φωτός' matching 'children of the light of truth'; added identification per rule. Title names the thought (where the shepherd is, there follow). Notes disclose OCR/variant status (none present). Covered source paragraphs: [1]. No uncertainties or contradictions between Pass A/B and Greek.
